dataset_name: API Behavioral Contracts & Deontic Modalities Corpus (APIstic Mined)
dataset_source: APIstic: Large-Scale OpenAPI Evolution Dataset (ACM MSR 2024 / Zenodo 20525072)
description: Comprehensive corpus of API behavioral rules, deontic contracts, and consumer breakage risk clauses mined from real-world OpenAPI commits for training Student 3's Behavioral Classifier.

train_samples.clause: Mandatory: caller must provide warehouse id in request parameters.
The client must include a valid Idempotency-Key header on all POST requests.
Every user account creation shall require two-factor authentication verification.
Clients must supply an authorization bearer token signed by an approved identity provider.
Caller must specify ISO-4217 three-letter currency code in transaction payload.
Request must contain valid signature generated with shared HMAC secret.
Clients are required to send Accept: application/json in HTTP headers.
All requests must supply an X-Consumer-Username header.
The application shall encrypt payload fields using AES-256 before transmission.
Mandatory requirement: client must explicitly confirm terms of service version.
Consumers must provide callback webhook URL for asynchronous notifications.
Caller must include client_id and client_secret in basic auth credentials.
All batch requests must provide an explicit batch_size integer.
Clients must pass non-empty order item array on checkout.
Consumers are obligated to verify server SSL certificates.
Clients must not send more than 10 requests per second under penalty of HTTP 429.
Callers are strictly forbidden from reusing an expired session token.
Third-party applications must never query inactive inventory without explicit permission.
Do not execute concurrent write operations on the same resource ID.
Consumers must not store raw credit card numbers on local storage.
Payload size must not exceed 2 megabytes.
Callers are prohibited from invoking administration endpoints via public internet.
Do not pass cleartext passwords in URL query parameters.
Clients must not initiate more than 3 simultaneous file export jobs.
Users may not cancel subscriptions that have already entered the billing settlement phase.
Do not cache responses flagged with Cache-Control: no-store.
Applications must never bypass certificate pin validations.
Clients must not send empty JSON objects in POST request body.
Never submit payment requests with negative currency amounts.
Callers are forbidden from modifying system-managed audit timestamps.
Consumers may optionally include an expand parameter to retrieve nested entities.
Callers can provide an optional trace_id for distributed tracing telemetry.
Clients may request results in either JSON or XML format using the Accept header.
Developers are allowed to test endpoints against the sandbox environment freely.
System may cache successful GET responses for up to 60 seconds.
Callers may filter records using standard SQL wildcards.
Clients can omit the customer description field if unknown.
Consumers may compress request bodies using gzip transfer encoding.
Users are permitted to fetch up to 1000 items per request in bulk mode.
Callers may provide an optional client reference identifier.
Clients can optionally request asynchronous webhook dispatching.
Developers may inspect deprecation timelines via OpenAPI headers.
Consumers may issue HEAD requests to inspect content length headers.
Clients can supply multiple email recipients separated by commas.
Users are allowed to override default pagination ordering.
Account balance must be greater than zero before submitting withdrawal.
Order status must be in PENDING_PAYMENT before invoking capture endpoint.
Cart must contain at least one physical item prior to calculating shipping options.
User must verify email address before accessing personal identifiable information.
Users must agree to terms of service before generating an API key.
Resource must be in DRAFT state prior to triggering publication workflow.
Customer account must have verified billing method before subscribing.
Caller must acquire distributed lock on resource before initiating batch update.
Session must be initialized via OAuth authorization code grant first.
Previous transaction must have settled prior to issuing charge reversal.
Webhook target endpoint must respond with HTTP 200 to validation ping.
User must hold role ADMIN to execute tenant deletion operations.
Device must complete biometric authentication before token refresh.
Invoice must be unpaid prior to applying discount code.
Cluster node must be cordoned before issuing drain command.
Guarantees database write is committed before HTTP 200 response is returned.
Order creation guarantees immediate debit from the customer wallet balance.
Returns exact real-time snapshot with read-after-write consistency guaranteed.
Operation is strictly asynchronous; callers must poll task URL for completion status.
Guarantees resource is purged from all replica caches upon 204 No Content.
Successful payment execution generates audit record and dispatches email receipt.
Response guarantees transaction rollback on any downstream microservice timeout.
Endpoint returns HTTP 202 Accepted; consumer must poll job endpoint for artifacts.
Operation guarantees idempotency: replaying request yields identical receipt.
Server promises persistent retention of webhook event payload for 30 days.
Job enqueued asynchronously; completion notification sent via registered webhook.
Ensures row lock is released immediately following response dispatch.
Returns newly created resource representation with populated ID and timestamps.
Guarantees event publication to Kafka broker with at-least-once delivery.
Operation will trigger background index recomputation across elasticsearch nodes.
Maximum rate limit enforced: 100 requests per minute per IP address.
Rate limit restricted to 20 calls per minute for unauthenticated public clients.
API quota capped at 10,000 monthly transactions per API key.
Burst capacity limited to 5 concurrent connections per tenant.
Requests exceeding 50 calls per second are throttled with HTTP 429 response.
Search queries restricted to 5 calls per minute per user account.
Hard quota enforced: 500 requests per day for developer tier accounts.
Bulk export endpoint rate limited to 2 executions per hour.
File upload throughput limited to 10 MB per minute per API key.
Callers exceeding rate quota will receive Retry-After header with wait duration.
Concurrency limit capped at 10 simultaneous in-flight HTTP connections.
Global rate limit tightened to 60 calls per minute across all endpoints.
Token generation requests throttled to 3 attempts per 15 minutes.
Traffic capped at 500 MB bandwidth consumption per billing cycle.
Hourly quota reduced from 5000 to 1000 requests per tenant.

test_samples.clause: Mandatory: caller must pass tenant_id in request headers.
Caller must supply valid webhook HMAC signature.
Clients are required to provide billing email on account registration.
All API requests shall include an Authorization Bearer JWT.
Caller must supply idempotency key on financial transfer requests.
Every batch update must provide non-empty record list.
Clients must not issue duplicate request tokens within 5 minutes.
Do not pass unencrypted passwords over non-TLS connections.
Clients are strictly prohibited from sharing API access keys.
Consumers must not query database replica during failover maintenance.
Do not exceed maximum payload length of 1000 characters.
Third-party callers are forbidden from invoking administrative endpoints.
Callers can optionally request gzip compressed transfer encoding.
Callers may provide page and limit query parameters for pagination.
Clients are permitted to cache static metadata for 24 hours.
Users may optionally provide an external transaction identifier.
Consumers can request response bodies in protocol buffer format.
Developers are allowed to test endpoints against staging server freely.
Resource must be unlocked before issuing delete request.
User profile must have verified phone number prior to money transfer.
Order must be marked as SHIPPED before submitting tracking number.
Consumers must not initiate withdrawal if account balance is negative.
Clients can execute payments only after completing identity registration.
Client must acquire valid OAuth token before invoking user data endpoint.
Response guarantees immediate SMS delivery before socket close.
Endpoint returns HTTP 202 Accepted; caller must poll status endpoint until job terminates.
Guarantees immediate database consistency upon 200 OK return.
Operation queues background image resize job; status returned asynchronously.
Operation promises persistent cloud storage sync within 5 seconds.
Guarantees resource record deletion across all backup clusters.
Rate limit throttled to 5 requests per second.
Quota capped at 100 API calls per hour per user account.
Burst concurrency restricted to 3 simultaneous HTTP requests.
Throttling enforced: maximum 500 requests per minute.
Monthly usage quota reduced to 50,000 queries.
Server promises that rate limit will not exceed 100 requests per minute.
